subject: Dedicated capacity options & ramp plan
messages:
From: Caroline Hayes <caroline@opsai.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity options & ramp plan

Diego —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We loved Redwood's latency guarantees and the autoscaling behavior, but before we move forward I need a couple of concrete reservation options to take to procurement: minimum GPUs (per region), suggested ramp schedule from pilot to prod, and an estimate of month-to-month cost for each phase.

Quick context on OpsAI workload:
- Models: mixture of a 6B chat model and a small LLM for embeddings/semantic search.
- Target production load in 90 days: ~120 concurrent chat sessions, median 50 tokens/turn, mix of short back-and-forths (5-7 turns).
- Latency SLO: 300ms p50 for chat inference, p95 under 800ms.
- Burstiness: spikes for 30–45 minutes during customer webinars (up to 2.5x baseline).

We want an approach that keeps first costs small (pilot) but gives a clear path to predictable throughput for launch. Please include any assumptions you need (token distribution, batching, multi-model placement).

Also flag any minimum commitment required to get the SLA and what warm-pool/warmup windows you recommend.

Thanks —
Caroline
VP Product, OpsAI
caroline@opsai.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Hayes <caroline@opsai.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options & ramp plan

Caroline —

Really helpful context, thank you. Attached is a concise set of reservation options (opsai_dedicated_options_v1.pdf) that map to Pilot, Onramp, and Production stages. High level:

1) Pilot (4-GPU reserved lane) — purpose: integration and SLA validation
   - 4 x NVIDIA A100 equivalent (shared burst pool across two AZs)
   - Expected steady throughput: ~30 concurrent sessions; p50 latency target achievable with light batching disabled
   - Duration recommendation: 2–4 weeks

2) Onramp (8-GPU minimum reserved) — purpose: controlled ramp and early production
   - 8 x A100 equiv reserved (2 AZs for redundancy) + 8-GPU burst allowance (pay-as-you-go)
   - Expected steady: 60–80 concurrent sessions with quantized 6B model; autoscale handles temporary spikes
   - Warm-pool: keep 2 GPUs pre-warmed for model loads with 15–30 min warmup latency

3) Production (24-GPU reserve, burst to 40) — purpose: full launch & webinars
   - 24 x reserved GPUs split across 3 AZs, hot-standby for failover; burst policy to 40 GPUs for short windows
   - Expected steady: 120 concurrent sessions with targeted p95 below 800ms assuming token optimization and prefix KV caching

Assumptions included in the attachment: token mix, request concurrency model, model memory after 4-bit quantization on the 6B model, and a 1.2x headroom multiplier for tail latency. I also included a short notes doc on SLA prerequisites (SLA requires a minimum 8-GPU reserved floor to guarantee latencies beyond pilot).

I've cc'd Kimberly to add any technical throughput notes and Ben for pricing and deal guidance. We can adjust the ramp days or the floor if you prefer a more gradual taper.

Next steps: if this looks directionally correct, we can lock a pilot credit + onramp discount while Ops finalizes procurement. I'll follow up with a pricing worksheet and a proposed commit schedule.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachments: opsai_dedicated_options_v1.pdf, Redwood_Dedicated_Terms_v1.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Caroline Hayes <caroline@opsai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options & ramp plan

Caroline / Diego —

A few technical clarifications to bake into any reservation:
- Batching profile: OpsAI's chat workload (short turns, frequent small messages) benefits less from large batching. Plan for lower batching gains: design throughput around minimal batching (2–3 tokens aggregated).
- KV/prefix caching: with a warmed KV cache we estimate ~20–25% token-cost reduction and improved p95. Keep cache residency across hot GPUs where possible.
- Quantization: target 4-bit quant; that brings the 6B model memory down to ~10–12 GB and allows 3–4 concurrent streams per GPU for low-latency inference.
- Minimum sustained utilization: for cost efficiency and SLA we recommend a 65% sustained utilization target on reserved GPUs; that suggests an 8-GPU minimum for early prod rather than 4.
- Warmup strategy: staggered warm pools per AZ to limit cross-AZ cold starts during spikes. Warm pool hold: 15–45 minutes depending on burst pattern.

I've put a simple throughput estimator as an attachment (throughput_estimator.csv) that converts your session counts and token assumptions into GPU-hours. If you want, I can run this with OpsAI telemetry to produce a tuned ramp schedule.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachments: throughput_estimator.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Hayes <caroline@opsai.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Feb 2027 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options & ramp plan

Caroline —

Thanks for looping us in. Based on Diego/Kim's notes, here's a pricing sketch and a few commercial options we can present to procurement:

A) Month-to-month pilot (no term)
   - 4 GPU reserved lane + pay-go burst: list $/GPU-hr applied; no SLA commitment. Pilot credit: $10k credit applied to first invoice.

B) 6–12 month onramp (recommended)
   - 8-GPU reserved floor, sliding burst to 24 for the ramp period. 10% discount for 6-mo, 18% for 12-mo.

C) Annual production commit (best unit economics)
   - 24-GPU reserved with burst to 40, 22–30% discount tiers with ramp credits and a one-time onboarding credit to offset migration effort.

We can structure a staircase commitment: start at 8 GPUs month 1–3, step to 16 GPUs months 4–6, then 24 GPUs months 7+. We'd bake in a 60-day notice window for down-scaling and provide a 2-week activation SLA for any added reserved lanes.

Deal ID: RDW-2027-OPS-042 (for procurement reference). Attached is a pricing workbook (OpsAI_pricing_v1.xlsx) with modeled invoice lines for the three options.

If Ops procurement needs a shorter payment window or PO terms, we can flex the discount slightly. Happy to hop on a call with your procurement team to walk numbers.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachments: OpsAI_pricing_v1.xlsx

Caroline —

To align expectations on the operational side, here's a proposed onboarding cadence tied to the commercial choices above:

- Kickoff (week 0): architecture review, credentials, and network allowlist — 1 full day.
- Pilot activation (weeks 1–2): small reserved lane active; integration tests, basic observability dashboards enabled.
- Onramp phase (weeks 3–6): scaling patterns validated, canary traffic, performance tuning.
- Production activation (week 7+): switch traffic and standby runbook drills; post-launch 30-day health check.

We're keeping an "activation buffer" of 48 hours for provisioning reserved lanes (subject to capacity availability in your target region). I'll attach a kickoff agenda (onboarding_kickoff_agenda.docx) and create a shared folder for runbooks.

DocuSign link for a standard 12-month commit (if you want the onramp discounts): https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123-opsai-reservation
Kickoff doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/opsai-kickoff

Thanks — looking forward to partnering.

-Lauren
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick engagement from your side. To summarize and confirm next steps:

1) We'll proceed with the recommended onramp staircase: 8 GPUs (month 1–3) -> 16 GPUs (month 4–6) -> 24 GPUs (month 7+). That preserves the SLA and meets your p50/p95 targets when combined with Kim's quantization & caching notes.
2) Ben will send a formal quote and include a pilot credit ($10k) applied to the first invoice. Deal ID: RDW-2027-OPS-042.
3) Lauren will schedule the kickoff; proposed kickoff doc is linked above.
4) I'll share the two attachments (opsai_dedicated_options_v1.pdf, Redwood_Dedicated_Terms_v1.pdf) and the DocuSign link for signature. Please let me know if procurement needs a different PO flow — we can accommodate net-30 or net-45 with a small cadence change to the discount.

If that all looks good, I can have the paperwork out today so we can hit pilot activation the week after signature.

Best,
